q: Who is sent to T'Telir to marry the God King of Hallandren?
explain: Siri, the youngest princess of Idris, is sent in place of her older sister Vivenna.

q: From which kingdom do Siri and Vivenna come?
explain: Idris is a small, austere highland kingdom north of Hallandren.

q: What is the capital city of Hallandren?
explain: T'Telir is a colorful coastal city that houses the Court of Gods.

q: Lightsong is worshipped in Hallandren as the god of what?
explain: Ironically, Lightsong doubts his own divinity and prefers jokes to heroics.

q: What is the purpose Nightblood was Awakened to fulfil?
explain: Nightblood has no clear idea of what evil actually is, which makes it terribly dangerous.

q: Why is the God King Susebron unable to speak?
wrong: He took a vow of silence
explain: His priests removed his tongue so he could never use his vast store of Breath to Awaken.

q: Who serves as Lightsong's high priest?
explain: Lightsong nicknames the patient Llarimar "Scoot".

q: Who is the king of Idris and father of Siri and Vivenna?
explain: Dedelin sends Siri instead of Vivenna, hoping to keep his heir-trained daughter safe.

q: Which mercenary leader works for Vivenna in T'Telir?
explain: Denth seems a friendly hireling, but he is secretly working to start the war.

q: Besides Breath, what does Awakening draw from nearby objects?
explain: Objects used as a source of color turn grey once the Awakening is done.

q: In Hallandren, what is a person called who has no Breath at all?
explain: Drabs see colors as duller and are often shunned by others.

q: What are the Lifeless that make up Hallandren's armies?
explain: Lifeless can be created with a single Breath and follow simple Commands.

q: What can members of the Idrian royal family do with their hair?
explain: The Royal Locks shift color with emotion, which Siri struggles to control.

q: What do the Returned usually lose when they come back from death?
explain: Returned keep only vague dreams and impressions of who they were.

q: Which princess had been betrothed to the God King since birth?
explain: Vivenna trained her whole life for the marriage, only to see Siri sent instead.

q: What is the name of the god worshipped in Idris?
explain: Austrism teaches humility and frowns on bright colors and ostentation.

q: Blushweaver is the Hallandren goddess of what?
explain: Blushweaver uses her political cunning to push the Court of Gods toward war with Idris.

q: To which people does the palace scribe Bluefingers belong?
explain: Bluefingers plots a war between Hallandren and Idris to free the Pahn Kahl.

q: How often must a Returned absorb a new Breath to stay alive?
explain: Hallandren citizens donate these Breaths, which keep the gods' Divine Breath going.

q: How many Heightenings of Breath are there?
explain: The Tenth Heightening requires around 50,000 Breaths, a level held by the God King.

q: How does Lightsong save Susebron at the climax of Warbreaker?
explain: The gift heals Susebron's tongue but costs Lightsong his life.

q: Which legendary figure who ended the Manywar is revealed to be Vasher?
explain: Peacegiver ended the war by giving his treasure of Breath to the line of God Kings.

q: Where are Kalad's Phantoms secretly hidden in T'Telir?
explain: The Phantoms are Lifeless made of bones encased in stone, posing as statues.

q: Shashara, Vasher's former lover, was the sister of which mercenary?
explain: Vasher killed Shashara, which fuels Denth's hatred of him.

q: On Roshar, Vasher goes by Zahel. What does he do for Adolin?
explain: Zahel is a sharp-tongued ardent and dueling master in the Kholin warcamp.
source: Words of Radiance; Words of Brandon

q: Under what name does Vivenna appear in Kholinar in Oathbringer?
explain: Vivenna travelled to Roshar and, in Kholinar, became known as the swordswoman Azure.

q: Which Awakener created Nightblood together with Vasher?
explain: The two Awakened the sword together; Vasher later killed Shashara with it to keep the method of Awakening steel secret.

q: In the prologue, from which imprisoned rebel does Vasher obtain Breath?
explain: Vahr had led a rebellion against Hallandren and hoarded Breath before his capture.

q: What are the Tears of Edgli, a major source of Hallandren's wealth?
explain: Their vibrant dyes fuel the color trade that makes Hallandren rich.

q: Which dying Idrian spy passes his large store of Breath to Vivenna?
explain: Lemex was being secretly poisoned by Denth, and the sudden Breath leaves Vivenna overwhelmed.

q: Who is the high priest of the God King Susebron?
explain: Treledees dies defending Siri and Susebron during the Pahn Kahl rebellion.

q: How do Siri and Susebron first manage to talk to each other?
explain: Their secret written conversations happen at night in the God King's bedchamber.

q: As one of the Five Scholars, Vasher was known by what name?
explain: As Talaxin, he created Nightblood together with Shashara.

q: Clod, the Lifeless in Denth's crew, was once which of the Five Scholars?
explain: Arsteel was killed by Vasher in a duel and later turned into a Lifeless.

q: Which of the Five Scholars discovered ichor-alcohol for Lifeless?
explain: Ichor-alcohol replaces a Lifeless's blood and makes it far more durable.

q: Mercystar, whose palace is broken into, is the goddess of what?
explain: Blushweaver uses the break-in to persuade Mercystar to join her preparations for war.

q: Who is the Vessel of the Shard Endowment?
explain: Her name lives on in the Tears of Edgli, the flowers behind Hallandren's dyes.

q: Which Heightening makes an Awakener stop aging?
explain: It takes about 2,000 Breaths, and every Returned enjoys its benefits automatically.

q: How did the man who became Lightsong die?
explain: In life he was Stennimar, the brother of his future high priest Llarimar.

q: What is the capital city of Idris?
explain: Bevalis is a small city in a mountain valley, modest beside Hallandren's capital.

q: Vasher, Shashara, Arsteel and Yesteel were four of the Five Scholars. Who was the fifth?
explain: Denth, who later led a band of mercenaries in T'Telir, was also a Returned and one of the Five Scholars.

q: What color do Siri's Royal Locks turn when she is frightened?
explain: Red shows anger or embarrassment, and black is the calm, controlled color Idrian royals are trained to keep.

q: Lightsong holds the Command phrases for how many of Hallandren's Lifeless?
explain: Each of four gods holds the phrases for a quarter of the Lifeless army.

q: Which Command lets an Awakener take back the Breath stored in an object they Awakened?
explain: The Awakener must touch the object; "My life to yours, my Breath become yours" is the Command that gives Breath away.

q: Why is the palace scribe Bluefingers given that nickname?
a: His fingers are stained with ink
wrong: He handles the palace's blue dyes
He lost his fingers to frostbite
explain: His fingers seem permanently stained with blue ink, and he is rarely seen without his ledger.

q: Which colors do Lightsong, his priests and his servants wear?
explain: Each Returned god of Hallandren has their own colors, worn by everyone in their service.

q: On what basis do the kings of Idris claim the right to rule Hallandren?
a: They are its royal line from before the Manywar
wrong: They hold Peacegiver's treasure of Breath
Austre crowned them after the Manywar
explain: The royal family fled to the highlands when Hallandren chose to be ruled by the Returned.

q: Lightsong gives his Lifeless Command phrases to another Returned, who surprises him by handing over her own. Who?
explain: With both sets of phrases, Lightsong suddenly controls half of Hallandren's Lifeless army.

q: Which Heightening grants perfect pitch?
explain: It takes about 200 Breaths; the Third Heightening adds perfect color recognition.

q: At which Heightening can an Awakener use basic Commands instinctively, without any training?
explain: The Sixth Heightening requires about 3,500 Breaths.

q: Roughly how many Breaths are needed to reach the First Heightening?
explain: The First Heightening grants aura recognition and a stronger life sense.

q: How many Breaths went into Awakening Nightblood?
explain: Awakening steel required forging the Breaths into the blade along with an extremely difficult visualization.

q: Lightsong keeps dreaming of a red panther. What was the Red Panther in his former life?
explain: Llarimar borrowed the Red Panther for a family trip, and Lightsong later uses its name as a Command phrase.

q: Who was the first Returned, who proclaimed the Five Visions and died again a week later?
explain: Hoid tells his story at the Court of Gods; the Five Visions became the core of Austrism.

q: According to Hoid's tale, who was chosen as the first monarch after Vo, beginning the line of the Idrian royals?
explain: Vo's shipmates founded a kingdom and made his wife, who carried his child, their queen; her line later ruled Idris.

q: Hopefinder the Just is the Hallandren god of what?
explain: Hopefinder is one of the four gods who hold the Command phrases of the Lifeless army.

q: Kalad the Usurper, whose name lives on in Kalad's Phantoms, was actually whom?
explain: As Kalad, Vasher created the Phantoms during the Manywar, long before he was revered as Peacegiver.

q: What do Idrians call the body of water that Hallandren calls the Bright Sea?
explain: Landlocked Idris downplays the sea that lets T'Telir thrive as a port.

q: What is the name of the Hallandren religion that worships the Returned as gods?
explain: The Iridescent Tones teach that only those who die exemplifying a great virtue are sent back as Returned.

q: What is the real name of the palace scribe known as Bluefingers?
explain: He introduces himself to Siri by this name, adding that everyone calls him Bluefingers.
